title: Fulton County Mobile Health Clinic 4-Saturday Equity Deployment Plan
van_profile: 1 Van, 1 Nurse Practitioner, Blood Pressure Cuff, Glucometer, ~40 Patients/Day

section_1_planner.overall_logistics_summary: Selected 4 sites balancing vehicle turning radius (25 ft), paved lot staging, and pedestrian foot traffic across diverse Fulton County sectors. Each site accommodates a 24-ft mobile clinic van, patient intake canopy, and safe triage zone.

location_audits.audit_findings: CONVENIENCE MISMATCH: Uninsured rate is only 4.1% and private care is 0.2 miles away. Selected primarily for ample parking capacity rather than clinical necessity.
Strong equity target. Tract has 24.8% uninsured rate and residents face 68-minute transit travel time with 3 bus transfers to reach safety-net care.
Strong equity target. Tract has 22.5% uninsured rate and residents face 58-minute transit travel time with 2 bus transfers to reach safety-net care.
Strong equity target. Tract has 25.2% uninsured rate and residents face 35-minute transit travel time with 1 bus transfers to reach safety-net care.

section_2_auditor.convenience_vs_need_verdict: CONVENIENCE BIAS DETECTED: 1 of 4 sited locations exhibit low healthcare barriers. The Planner favored spacious parking aprons over documented healthcare deserts.
recommended_adjustments: Vine City / English Avenue (26.1% uninsured, 38m transit)

section_3_communicator.general_community_announcement:
FREE COMMUNITY HEALTH CHECKUPS IN FULTON COUNTY THIS MONTH!

A mobile health clinic van is coming to your neighborhood on Saturdays from 9 AM to 3 PM. A friendly Nurse Practitioner will check your blood pressure and blood sugar, answer your health questions, and give you healthy tips. Everything is completely FREE. You do not need health insurance, money, or an ID card. Walk-ups are welcome—first come, first served for up to 40 neighbors each Saturday. See our schedule below!

section_4_limitations.ecological_fallacy_risk: Census tracts in Fulton County average 4,000 residents across diverse micro-environments. Attributing tract-level uninsured rates (e.g. 28.4%) to every household within the boundary commits an ecological fallacy. Pockets of severe uninsurance can exist in moderate-income tracts, and well-insured clusters can exist in high-vulnerability tracts.
section_4_limitations.spatial_resolution_gap: Geographic coordinates with 4 decimal places provide theoretical precision of approximately 11.1 meters (~36 feet). However, numerical GPS coordinates do not encode ground-truth curb realities: curb cut heights, active loading zone tow ordinances, low-hanging utility wires, generator noise ordinances, or private property towing enforcement. Ground-truthed physical scouting is essential.
section_4_limitations.transit_schedule_discrepancy: Published General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) travel times assume on-time bus schedules. In practice, Saturday MARTA headways frequently experience 30-to-60 minute intervals, missed connections, and service cuts. Transit times reported here (e.g. 52-68 minutes) represent optimistic lower bounds; actual patient transit burden is frequently 1.5x to 2x greater.
section_4_limitations.uninsured_rate_recency: American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year rolling estimates lag real-time policy shocks. Specifically, Georgia's ongoing Medicaid redetermination ('unwinding') and shifts in low-income safety net qualification mean current uninsured numbers may exceed survey baselines by 15-25% in high-churn working class tracts.
